name: @atusy/tsudoi-language-server
//exports: SUPERSEDES the note this key carried through sprint 9, which said an installed copy CANNOT run under deno and that main/bin belong elsewhere. That is now false: this package ships COMPILED .js built by prepack, and deno's restriction is on type-STRIPPING under node_modules, not on running .js from there. The published surface is dist/ alone -- src/ is deliberately NOT shipped, so no user can aim a runtime at a .ts entry point under node_modules and hit that error at all. There is still no `main`, no `.` export and no `bin`. The map's three arms and the reason for each, the refusal of `bin`, and why JSR was measured and declined are asserted in test/package-shape.test.ts: package.json cannot carry comments, oxfmt sorts this key to the tail, and a test is the one home for a reason that fails when someone violates it.
//no-readme: THIS PACKAGE SHIPS NO README AND THAT IS A RULING RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. A member README exists for the one reader who has only that document -- and this package's reader does not arrive that way: the sole documented route to its tarball IS the root README's quickstart, so they have already read it. Two of the four facts a handler README owes (the peer on tsudoi, the link `bun install` does not create) are unstatable by this package about itself, so test/readme.test.ts enumerates HANDLER packages rather than members. A prose-only pointer is refused on this repository's doctrine that the document nobody executes is the one that goes stale. WHAT IT COSTS, FILED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: a pack here produces a tarball with no README, which binds only the day this package publishes -- and `private` above forecloses that until a publishing decision reopens it.
//private: THIS IS THE MANIFEST WHOSE EDIT PERMITS PUBLICATION, and the key is the machine gate every handler's optional-peer flag is carried under: `bun publish` refuses a private package before `prepack` is even run. MEASURED on bun 1.3.13 that the gate is THIS file's and not the workspace root's -- a publish run inside a member with `private` deleted here packs and reaches authentication while the root still carries the key. test/optional-peer-premise.test.ts LOCATES this manifest by the name it declares, so deleting the key reddens both handlers; the workspace root's own permanent `private: true` cannot stand in for it and is not read.
